How does this bookshelf work ? let say my skill are 45/45 i store 5 skills so it will be 40/45 ?

before all that i should ask this store SKILLS right ? not recipe ?

comments.author: Visitor
comments.body:
Yes, this item allows you to store character SKILLS, not recipes. Stored skills are unusable while stored, but it is better than deleting a skill and losing all your progress; they can be retrieved at any time from your quarters, or from a Scholar in any city throughout the world.

But the storage process takes one twenty-four hour day per skill rank level, and you can neither use nor recover a skill that is in the process of being stored during that time.

Perhaps this link would be of use to you: nforum.ogplanet.com/uwo/forum_posts.asp?TID=641808

Use Ctrl-F to find "5-A." -- it is a section that covers Skill Bookshelves in slightly greater depth than I have done here, with screenshots included for easier reference.

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
1: I've replaced other pieces of furniture without losing their contents, so I'm sure the same principle would apply here. The new furniture simply overwrites the previous furniture without contents being destroyed, though be sure you replace it with a similar kind (5-shelf replaced with 5-shelf) or a superior one (4-shelf replaced with 5-shelf) to avoid losing the extra storage slot. Furniture can have its durability restored with Master's Repair Tools items as well.

2: I'm not so sure about that. Never let any of my pieces of furniture break with something still inside them, Bookshelf or otherwise. It'd be easy enough to test with a cheap +1 slot furniture item for trade goods or something, and then store items until it breaks, I guess... you do get a notification each time durability points reach certain levels, typically every 5 points, and equipment/furniture informs you about its durability every time a point is lost when it hits 5 durability or below. So it's really hard to lose something to durability hitting 0 without having sufficient warning.

I tested furniture breakage! With a +2 item furniture add-on, but it was quicker and cheaper than a Bookshelf, and less risky.
